Query Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__cloud_sql.R
oauth_db_cloud_sql_postgres.Rd

Open a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL connection with the visitor's Google access token as the IAM database password. Queries work with DBI and dbplyr.

Usage

oauth_db_cloud_sql_postgres(
  authorization,
  host,
  dbname,
  user,
  ...,
  port = 5432L,
  hostaddr = NULL,
  sslrootcert = NULL,
  sslcert = NULL,
  sslkey = NULL,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/sqlservice.login",
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

host

One database hostname matching its TLS server certificate.

dbname

Database name.

user

IAM database username, or a function returning it for the selected account. For a Google user, this is their full email address. The server checks that the token belongs to that IAM identity.

...

RPostgres options: bigint, check_interrupts, timezone, timezone_out, connect_timeout, application_name, or TCP keepalives (keepalives, keepalives_idle, keepalives_interval, keepalives_count, tcp_user_timeout). Authentication and TLS settings cannot be overridden.

port

Database TCP port.

hostaddr

Optional server IP address. host still supplies the name checked against the certificate.

sslrootcert

Trusted server CA certificate file, or NULL for libpq's configured trust store.

sslcert, sslkey

Optional client certificate and private key files. Supply both if the instance requires a client certificate.

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

OAuth scopes to check before opening a connection. Defaults to Google's Cloud SQL login scope. Set explicitly when a custom client uses an alternative accepted scope; this check doesn't grant IAM or database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A reactive function returning a native RPostgres DBI connection.

Details

Enable Cloud SQL IAM database authentication, add the user's IAM account or group, grant Cloud SQL Instance User, and grant SQL privileges separately. Use oauth_db_cloud_sql_client() for Google sign-in. The app host needs a direct network route to the instance and a hostname matching its certificate. Shared or customer-managed server CAs can provide such DNS names; see the source guide for per-instance CA restrictions.

Install RPostgres linked to libpq 16 or later. Connections require password authentication and verified TLS (sslmode = "verify-full"), with GSS encryption disabled. Unset PGSERVICE and PGSERVICEFILE; connection service files cannot supply alternative settings.

Create the helper inside server() and get connection <- con() before each operation. When the token changes, the next con() call closes the old connection and opens one with current credentials. Ordinary renewal doesn't replay completed reactive queries. Finish a transaction on the connection that started it. Account changes, permission loss, sign-out and session end close the managed connection.

The helper uses manual IAM database authentication with visitor tokens. It doesn't use a proxy's automatic IAM login or the hosting account's credentials. Cloud SQL MySQL and SQL Server aren't supported by this helper.

See also

oauth_db_cloud_sql_client(). vignette("cloud-sql", package = "shinyOAuthDB").

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- oauth_db_cloud_sql_postgres(
  auth$connection, host = "db.example.org", dbname = "reporting",
  user = "analyst@example.org", sslrootcert = "server-ca.pem"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT current_user")
})
} # }
